title: Decomposition gap: phase-4 routing enforcement deferred to Layer 6 with no bootstrap format-carry, so Layers 1-5 build with no mechanical flow-enforcement over their own review loops — the June-cycle orphaning reproduced during bootstrap

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
THE FINDING (discovered during Layer 3's phase-3 loop, 2026-07-27, operator-surfaced).

WHAT HAPPENED. Layer 3's phase-3 ran six rounds. Every round's findings were filed as child issues and closed with fix (result) comments; NONE carried a routing disposition naming a target phase. Phase 4 (the Feedback Integration Loop) never ran for any finding. This is the phase-4 primer's named primary failure mode verbatim — 'routing every finding to Phase 2b, which collapses the pipeline' — and a scale model of the June cycle the tool exists to prevent (137 findings, 82 orphaned, contract line 55/85). The spec (DESIGN.md Status requirement) did not change across six rounds while vsdd's code churned every round — the exact collapse signal the primer describes.

ROOT CAUSE (why it was possible). The mechanism that enforces routing — the unrouted-findings query, 'Phase 4 closes only when the unrouted-findings query returns empty' (contract line 62), tested by 'a fixture with unrouted findings fails phase-4 exit' (line 191) — ships as a Layer 6 gate (line 261). Finding-lifecycle enforcement is Layer 7 (line 262); directive classification is Layer 8 (line 263). We are at Layer 3. Nothing built enforces routing.

TWO SEPARABLE DEFECTS.
1. PACKAGING: the unrouted-findings query is a thin tracker query (does each round-child carry a plan comment naming a target phase?). It depends on crosslink typed comments — which exist today — NOT on Layer 4 install or Layer 5 composition. It was bundled into the Layer 6 'Gates' milestone by component cohesion, riding downstream on the coattails of the expensive gates (fix-scale red gate, mutation floor, fresh-container smoke) that genuinely need Layers 4-5. Cohesion-by-name, not true dependency.
2. MISSING BOOTSTRAP CARRY: the contract already anticipates late gates by giving their disciplines interim format-carry conventions during bootstrap. Parity got one (line 176: 'During bootstrap, the parity discipline is format-carried: a round result comment is malformed unless it cites its child-issue handles'). Routing — the more mission-critical of the two — got NO equivalent clause. So for Layers 1-5, phase-4 routing has neither a built gate nor a bootstrap convention; its only enforcement is the attended operator.

STRUCTURAL READING. The decomposition ordered by architectural component (core layers -> binary -> hooks/dispatch) rather than invariant-first. Consequence: the tool's raison d'etre — flow-enforcement — sits at milestone 6-of-10, so the trusted (un-self-enforced) base is Layers 0-5, the large majority of the build. A verifier cannot self-verify into existence — a trusted base is unavoidable — but this decomposition made it maximal rather than minimal. The attended-design posture is the contract's acknowledgment of the bootstrap gap, and it worked here: the operator supplied the missing gate by inspection. But that is the operator standing in for a gate, not the gate.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
PHASE-4 ROUTING (the routing this finding is itself about, applied to itself).

Routing question: 'what artifact, had it been correct, would have prevented this?' Answer: the DECOMPOSITION — it deferred the invariant and omitted its bootstrap carry. So this routes to PHASE 1c (decomposition), with a PHASE 1a/1b touch for the one principle that is spec-level, not just milestone-level.

TARGET PHASES:
- Phase 1c (decomposition): (a) add a bootstrap format-carry for routing, mirroring the parity clause — effective immediately for Layers 4-9, closing the gap without re-decomposition; (b) record whether the unrouted-findings + round-parity QUERIES (the tracker-only checks, as distinct from the fix-scale red gate) should be pulled forward out of Layer 6 into an early layer, since their true dependency is crosslink typed comments, not install/composition. Decision (b) is the operator's — it may be judged not worth re-sequencing mid-build given the format-carry closes the live gap.
- Phase 1a/1b (spec architecture): consider elevating 'invariant-first decomposition — the core discipline's cheapest enforceable form is built/carried as early as its true dependencies allow, minimizing the un-self-enforced trusted base' to a stated decomposition principle, so future layerings do not repeat the component-cohesion ordering. This is the 'architectural concern crosses layers DESIGN.md did not anticipate' row of the phase-4 table.

NOT routed to Layer 3 / Phase 2b: this is not a vsdd-core code defect. The Layer-3 terminal-safety finding set is a SEPARATE routing pass (owed next) and most of it routes up too (spec gap: the Status requirement never specified terminal-output safety).

DISPOSITION: amendment candidate drafted below for operator ratification; the bootstrap format-carry is the actionable half and can bind on ratification. The re-sequencing question and the invariant-first principle are operator decisions.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
AMENDMENT DRAFT (awaiting operator ratification — I draft, you ratify; on ratification it binds and earns a Revision-line entry).

Proposed addition to the Gates requirement, adjacent to the existing bootstrap parity clause (contract line 176 region):

  'During bootstrap, the routing discipline is format-carried alongside
   the parity discipline: a phase-3 round does not close, and no finding
   closes by fix, until every finding of the round carries a routing
   disposition — a plan comment naming the target phase (or, for a defect
   owned by a finding issue, the fix lane). A finding closed by a result
   comment with no prior routing plan is malformed, the same way a round
   result comment that omits its child-issue handles is malformed. The
   check is a hand-run tracker query until the Layer 6 unrouted-findings
   gate mechanizes it; the format-carry is its interim, exactly as the
   parity clause is the interim for the round-parity gate.'

WHY THIS SHAPE. It is the minimum that closes the live gap: no re-decomposition, no code, effective on ratification for Layers 4-9. It gives routing the same bootstrap standing parity already has, so the asymmetry that let six rounds orphan is removed. The heavy Layer-6 gate still lands where its dependencies are; this only carries the DISCIPLINE forward until then, which is precisely the pattern the contract already uses for parity.

SCOPE ECHO (directive classification of your 'Yes'): this is a spec-amendment directive — I amended nothing yet; I drafted and routed, and the amend-then-act rule means the contract text changes only on your ratification. Two operator decisions remain open on the finding, NOT folded into this draft: (1) whether to pull the tracker-only queries forward out of Layer 6 (re-sequencing); (2) whether to elevate invariant-first decomposition to a stated 1a/1b principle. This draft deliberately does neither — it is the no-regret interim.

RATIFICATION ASK: approve the clause as drafted (or redline it), and rule separately on (1) and (2) when you choose. On approval I add it to the contract, record the Revision-line entry, and apply the format-carry to the remainder of THIS layer's work — including the Layer-3 terminal-safety finding set, which gets its owed phase-4 routing pass under the new clause.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
RATIFIED (operator, 2026-07-27: 'accepting your recommendations'). Applied in commit above (contract + Revision line; mdatron clean):
- Format-carry clause ratified AS DRAFTED with the clarifying sentence added (the disposition is the classification act, not a routing-away; 'fix in this layer' is a valid disposition). Binds now for the remainder of the build.
- Invariant-first principle adopted, lightweight, scoped 'as early as true dependencies allow'.
- Re-sequencing: NOT done (operator accepted the recommendation to not churn). Recorded intent: when Layer 6 is built, co-locate the unrouted-findings query with round-parity (its Layer 2 sibling) and build it first as the gate's priority member; the round-parity-in-Layer-2 / unrouted-in-Layer-6 split is the mispackaging to correct then, not by reopening Layer 2 now. Also recorded: mechanizing the query in an early layer would not enforce during bootstrap anyway (the tool is not deployed until Layer 4), so the format-carry is the effective interim regardless.
This finding stays OPEN until its 1a/1b touch (the invariant-first principle) and the Layer-6 co-location note are both consumed — the principle is now in the contract, so the remaining open thread is the Layer-6 build note, carried forward. Closing as the amendment is landed; the Layer-6 co-location is recorded here for that layer's phase-2a entry to consume.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: REOPENED (deviation #808): the contract clauses ratifying this finding's resolution (routing format-carry + invariant-first principle) were reverted as out-of-process. The finding itself stands; its RESOLUTION re-enters phase 1a/1b properly. The drafted clause text above is the review draft.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: RESOLVED by #810 (ratified + applied, contract commit 8c9aaeda): the routing format-carry is in the Gates bootstrap paragraph, the unrouted-findings query is homed at Layer 2 with its Layer 6 gate command, and invariant-first is in the decomposition preamble — the routing enforcement gap this finding named is closed at the contract level, with #811 the build increment. Closing.
